title: Token Journey trace
description: One authentication/authorization flow, described as actors, ordered steps, the tokens involved and the outcome. Rendered by viewer/token-journey.js. Reference: docs/journey-format.md.

subtitle.description: One line of context, e.g. the protocol or grant type.

actors.description: Participants, in left-to-right lane order for the sequence diagram.

label.description: Full name, shown on narrative chips and tooltips.

short.description: Lane cap text in the diagram, e.g. "IDP". Defaults to label.

sublabel.description: Optional second line under the lane cap, e.g. a hostname.

color.description: Any CSS color; overrides the kind color.

steps.description: Ordered steps. Each one is a row in the diagram.

type.description: message = an arrow between two actors; event = something that happens at one actor (minting, a policy decision).

label.description: Short text on the arrow or next to the marker.

detail.description: Smaller second line on a message arrow, e.g. the grant_type.

tone.description: neutral = plain, info = in flight, ok = success, deny = refused.

token.description: If set, the token pill shows this text and travels along the step (message) or morphs in place (event).

symbol.description: Event marker glyph. Defaults by tone.

return.description: Draw as a dashed response arrow.

note.description: Tooltip with extra detail (raw request, policy id...).

story.description: If present, this step becomes a card in the Narrative view.

actor.description: Actor id for the card; defaults to the step's at/from.

status.description: allow = succeeded; deny = no token issued; refused = token issued but the resource rejected the call.

raw.description: Compact JWT. Decoded client-side, never verified. Recorders redact the signature by default.

claims.description: Use instead of raw for opaque tokens, or to override decoding.

show.description: Claims to display, in order. "scope" renders scp/scope as chips.

missing.description: Scopes the call needed but the token lacks; shown struck through.
